name: Nokia 5110 84x48 LCD (PCD8544)
description: Monochrome 84x48-pixel graphic LCD from the Nokia 5110/3310 phones, driven by a Philips PCD8544 controller over a write-only SPI-style serial bus (SCE, SCLK, SDIN, D/C, RES; 4 MHz max), with four backlight LEDs. The PCD8544 logic supply is 2.7-3.3 V and inputs must stay below VDD + 0.5 V, so run it from 3.3 V with 3.3 V logic. Sold as: Nokia 5110 LCD module, blue PCB printed "Nokia5110 3v-5v" (PCD8544, 8-pin header RST, CE, DC, DIN, CLK, VCC, BL, GND; the red clone has the same order with BL printed LIGHT).
eli5: A small old-phone screen that shows black text and simple pictures on a greenish background.

pins.name: RST
pins.description: Reset, active low (a reset pulse is required after power-up)

pins.name: DC
pins.description: Data/command: low = command, high = display data

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: Serial data in (SPI MOSI), sampled on the rising clock edge, MSB first

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 2.7-3.3 V (straight to the PCD8544, no regulator): use 3.3 V

pins.name: BL
pins.description: Backlight LEDs: drive high (3.3 V max, ideally through 330 ohm) for light, PWM to dim; leave open for no backlight

buildNotes: Power VCC from 3.3 V. The board is often printed "3v-5v", but the PCD8544 is rated 2.7-3.3 V with inputs up to VDD + 0.5 V and the module has no regulator or level shifter.

Apply a reset pulse after power-up (RST low >= 100 ns; the datasheet warns the chip can be damaged if it is not reset). Then send 0x21 (extended set), 0x04 (temperature coefficient), 0x13 (bias 1:48), 0x80|VOP (contrast), 0x20 (basic set), 0x0C (normal display).
Contrast VOP: VLCD = 3.06 + 0.06 x VOP volts. Keep VOP at or below 90 (VLCD max 8.5 V); 0x30-0x45 suits most panels. Too low = blank, too high = all dark.
RAM is 6 banks of 84 bytes, each byte a vertical strip of 8 pixels with the LSB on top: exactly MicroPython's framebuf.MONO_VLSB layout.
SPI mode 0, MSB first, at most 4 MHz; 2 MHz is safe on jumper wires. There is no MISO.
BL feeds the backlight LEDs. Use a 330 ohm series resistor from 3.3 V or a GPIO (PWM to dim); never 5 V straight in.

driver.code:
# MicroPython driver for the Philips PCD8544 84x48 mono LCD controller (Nokia 5110 module).
# Datasheet: Philips PCD8544 product specification, 1999 Apr 12.
# Write-only serial bus: SPI mode 0, MSB first, max 4 MHz. D/C low = command, high = display data.
import framebuf
from micropython import const
from time import sleep_ms

WIDTH = const(84)
HEIGHT = const(48)

# Instruction set (datasheet Table 1)
_FUNCTION_SET = const(0x20)   # 0 0 1 0 0 PD V H
_PD = const(0x04)             # power-down
_V = const(0x02)              # vertical addressing
_H = const(0x01)              # extended instruction set
_DISPLAY_CONTROL = const(0x08)  # H=0: 0 0 0 0 1 D 0 E
_DISPLAY_BLANK = const(0x08)
_DISPLAY_NORMAL = const(0x0C)
_DISPLAY_ALL_ON = const(0x09)
_DISPLAY_INVERSE = const(0x0D)
_SET_Y = const(0x40)          # H=0: bank 0..5
_SET_X = const(0x80)          # H=0: column 0..83
_TEMP_COEFF = const(0x04)     # H=1: TC1 TC0
_BIAS = const(0x10)           # H=1: BS2..BS0
_SET_VOP = const(0x80)        # H=1: VOP6..VOP0, VLCD = 3.06 + VOP * 0.06 V


class PCD8544(framebuf.FrameBuffer):
    """84x48 frame buffer; draw with the framebuf methods, then call show()."""

    def __init__(self, spi, cs, dc, rst=None, contrast=0x3F, bias=3, temp=0):
        # cs/dc/rst: Pin objects or GPIO numbers. contrast = VOP (0..127): keep VLCD <= 8.5 V,
        # i.e. VOP <= 90; 0x30..0x45 suits most modules. bias 3 = 1:48 mux (datasheet Table 4).
        from machine import Pin
        self.spi = spi
        self.cs = cs if isinstance(cs, Pin) else Pin(cs)
        self.dc = dc if isinstance(dc, Pin) else Pin(dc)
        self.rst = None if rst is None else (rst if isinstance(rst, Pin) else Pin(rst))
        self.cs.init(Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.dc.init(Pin.OUT, value=0)
        if self.rst is not None:
            self.rst.init(Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.buf = bytearray(WIDTH * HEIGHT // 8)
        # MONO_VLSB matches the PCD8544 RAM in horizontal addressing: byte = bank*84 + x, LSB on top.
        super().__init__(self.buf, WIDTH, HEIGHT, framebuf.MONO_VLSB)
        self._contrast = contrast & 0x7F
        self._bias = bias & 0x07
        self._temp = temp & 0x03
        self.reset()
        self.init_display()

    def reset(self):
        # Datasheet 8.1: a RES pulse is mandatory after power-on (RES LOW >= 100 ns).
        if self.rst is not None:
            self.rst(0)
            sleep_ms(1)
            self.rst(1)
            sleep_ms(1)

    def write_cmd(self, *cmds):
        self.dc(0)
        self.cs(0)
        self.spi.write(bytes(cmds))
        self.cs(1)

    def write_data(self, buf):
        self.dc(1)
        self.cs(0)
        self.spi.write(buf)
        self.cs(1)

    def init_display(self):
        # Datasheet Table 6 programming example, plus temperature coefficient and bias.
        self.write_cmd(
            _FUNCTION_SET | _H,               # PD=0, V=0, extended set
            _TEMP_COEFF | self._temp,
            _BIAS | self._bias,
            _SET_VOP | self._contrast,
            _FUNCTION_SET,                    # back to basic set, horizontal addressing
            _DISPLAY_NORMAL,
        )
        # RAM is undefined after power-on: clear it.
        self.fill(0)
        self.show()

    def contrast(self, vop):
        self._contrast = vop & 0x7F
        self.write_cmd(_FUNCTION_SET | _H, _SET_VOP | self._contrast, _FUNCTION_SET)

    def invert(self, on):
        self.write_cmd(_DISPLAY_INVERSE if on else _DISPLAY_NORMAL)

    def power_off(self):
        # Datasheet 8.3.1: fill the RAM with 0s before entering power-down.
        self.fill(0)
        self.show()
        self.write_cmd(_FUNCTION_SET | _PD)

    def power_on(self):
        self.init_display()

    def show(self):
        self.write_cmd(_SET_X | 0, _SET_Y | 0)
        self.write_data(self.buf)

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import sys
import time
from pcd8544 import PCD8544

# Pico: SPI0 pins. ESP32: any pins on SPI(2). PCD8544 max clock 4 MHz.
spi_id = 0 if sys.platform == 'rp2' else 2
spi = SPI(spi_id, baudrate=2000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({CLK}), mosi=Pin({DIN}))
lcd = PCD8544(spi, cs={CE}, dc={DC}, rst={RST})
n = 0
while True:
    lcd.fill(0)
    lcd.text('NOKIA', 0, 0, 1)
    lcd.text('Count ' + str(n), 0, 16, 1)
    lcd.show()
    print('count', n)
    n += 1
    time.sleep(1)
